proseChanges.summary: **Fixes — the every-minute scheduler, outbox delivery and message sends read only the work that is due:** on a large imported workspace with a growing outbox (every mail and chat message adds a row and none is ever removed), a backlog of workflow events waiting for a retry and tagged conversations, the scheduler's due-event pass and its refresh of rule and automation events, outbox delivery, a new conversation's live connection and each message's workflow and tag reads walked every outbox row, pending workflow event or tag link of the database: about 36,000 rows in a minute with nothing due, over a million once 20 events were due, and about 27,000 for each new chat's connection. They now search indexes of the undelivered outbox rows, the due and leased workflow events and each conversation's own tags, so this work reads about 15 rows in a minute with nothing due, under 50 for a message send and a handful for a new chat's connection, whatever the size of the outbox. The same events are claimed in the same order, the same messages are delivered in the same ticks, and every rule matches as before. One read is unchanged: the hourly pass of a time rule (such as closing solved tickets after four days) still reads the rule's whole status set, imported history included. The read of one conversation's pending workflow events and the bulk ticket workflow update read only the selected conversations' own events, in the same order as before, and the same rows are returned and updated. **Fixes — a re-crawled help site no longer makes conversations that cite its older pages walk the site:** deciding whether a cited page of an older crawl version is still current looks for a page of the published version at the same URL, and with no index holding that URL it read every page of the published version for each cited page whose URL is no longer published (about 2.6 million rows to open a conversation with 16 copied passages of 255 such pages on a large imported workspace). An index on a page's version and URL makes that lookup read only the pages at that URL. The decisions are unchanged. The same index would have made three lists that carry no explicit order come back in URL order instead of the order the pages were crawled: a dataset's pages list, which pages lexical search and the AI knowledge tool return among pages tied on score, and which 12 pages the customer-context catalog holds. They now state the crawl order (dataset, then the order its pages were stored) and read the same rows as before. **Fixes — opening a conversation no longer writes reference blocks:** until now every read of a conversation, thread or list also ran the copied-text check on the text it returned: it looked each passage of 12 or more words up in the knowledge index, refreshed that index when a help article had changed, and stored a reference block for each passage that matched a help article. On a large imported workspace that cost about 45 database statements and 27,000 rows read for one open, the stored blocks grew with reads alone, and the busy-database answer (503) showed up under load. A read now writes nothing and renders the references the stored text already holds, for each reader's current access, as before; the training-run artifact read and a live chat connection's replay of the messages it missed behave the same. Copied passages still become references when text is written (messages, notes, replies, saved replies, imports, pulls, mail), and the knowledge upgrade still does it for stored text. A Move in import step or a Zendesk pull step that lands articles now also brings the copied-text index current itself (up to 100 sources a step), which opening a conversation used to do as a side effect. What differs: text that was stored as plain words because it matched no help article when it was written, and matches one only now (an article published or edited later, for example a reply later turned into an article), is shown as stored to everyone who can read that conversation, instead of being replaced by "[Knowledge unavailable]" for a reader without access to that article; nothing stored changes. No migration. **Fixes — a conversation that holds references no longer reads every article of the workspace for each one, and a reference is found by its unique index:** when a teammate opens a conversation whose messages carry references (stored copies of help articles), the editor view looks up which articles each reference came from, and that lookup visited every article of the workspace (on a test workspace of 4,204 articles and 5,004 stored references, one open of a conversation with four references read about 36,000 rows). It now finds each article by its key (the same open reads about 2,400 rows; the lookup alone fell from 8,481 rows to 74). The lookup that stores a reference when text is written (messages, notes, replies, imports, answers) found its stored block by walking every block of the workspace and rescanning the request for each one; it now searches the unique workspace-and-fingerprint index once per block (35,312 rows read for six references among 5,004 blocks, now 14; a customer message that copies a help article reads about 3,800 rows instead of about 13,800). The rows returned, their order and every access check are unchanged, and a test runs the old and the new statements against the same data to prove it. What is not in this release: the conversation's attachment read still scans the attachment table, because no index covers the message it names; that needs a migration and waits for the next release. No migration. **rer 0.2.110 — the roster corner for a teammate erased by an older release is closed where HappyToHelp holds their hashed form, the managed-copy build issue REPORTS-001 is fixed, and the local key page changed:** the team adapter now names the older-release form of a roster address (`erased:` plus the SHA-256 of the lower-cased address, which v0.4.14 through v0.4.19 renamed an erased teammate's roster row to, and which v0.4.19 also stored as an inactive fence row at invite 0 for a teammate who was never on the roster), so a Business revision that lists a teammate erased by one of those releases by real address without a member id applies as retired (no fresh account, no invitation, no roster row) instead of the re-creation that the v0.4.20 and v0.4.21 notes describe as a known limit. What this does not cover: (1) a teammate erased before v0.4.14, which includes every teammate erased on production's v0.4.13 line, left no hashed form (the roster table first shipped in v0.4.14), so nothing recognises them from their address and a Business that lists them by address without a member id still creates a fresh account and an invitation; a Business that sends member ids fences them; (2) a teammate who was never on the roster and was erased by v0.4.19 is fenced only at invite 0, so a Business listing at invite 1 or higher admits them as a new person, as a larger invite number always does; (3) a person is recognised only under the address v0.4.19 stored for their roster row. The pin also fixes the managed-copy build (`rer check` no longer fails a managed copy of a published release for `.github/workflows` contract evidence it does not carry, REPORTS-001 on `.github/workflows/installer-journeys.yml`; proven on a synthetic managed copy with the platform's `rer-upstream.json`, not through a real platform build, and an install of an untagged commit keeps the check). The local key page (`/__dev/key`) now names the exact `rer dev` command to run, and the wording about the `/run` PATH changed; one known limit of that page: it tells a local owner who invited a teammate to run `rer dev --as <email>`, which HappyToHelp does not accept, because its local personas are the owner and signed-out only. Pins rer 0.2.110 and its Base copy. No migration. **Known limit — recovering an account that belongs to more than one workspace (still true in this release):** since v0.4.21 an owner changes a teammate's password or two-factor sign-in only where that workspace holds the account's sole membership. With outbound mail off (`MAIL_PROVIDER=none`), `/forgot-password` answers `503` for every account and sends nothing, so such an account cannot ask for a reset link by email, and the owner of either of its workspaces is refused with `409`; the deployer's hosted sign-in selects only an owner or an admin, so it does not help an operator-role teammate. An operator-role teammate in more than one workspace who has lost every second factor and recovery code has the same dead end with mail on or off, because `/forgot-password` changes only the password and an owner's two-factor reset is refused with `409` for such an account. The way out uses ordinary doors and keeps all support history (the removal drops the teammate's conversation follows and custom roles in that workspace, which its owner sets again): an owner of one of the account's workspaces removes it there (`DELETE /api/management/projects/<workspace id>/agents/<user id>`), the owner of the other workspace then issues the password-reset link or resets the two-factor sign-in, and the first workspace invites the teammate again. This release does not change the rule. **Correction to the v0.4.20 note on `rer deploy` and the mail secrets:** the v0.4.20 note said an offline `rer deploy --dry-run` lists the seven bound mail secret names and says the bound secrets were not read. That is what the dry-run prints with outbound mail off (`MAIL_PROVIDER=none`). Without any mail input (a new installation with `OWNER_EMAIL` only) it prints instead the production sign-in mail inputs a real deploy needs (`MAIL_PROVIDER`, `MAIL_FROM`, `EMAIL_API_KEY`) and still completes offline. Both shapes were run against this release's pinned rer 0.2.110: with `OWNER_EMAIL` only it printed that production sign-in mail line, and with `MAIL_PROVIDER=none` it printed "Outbound email is off (MAIL_PROVIDER=none) … The bound secrets were not read: if one of EMAIL_PROVIDER, EMAIL_FROM, EMAIL_API_KEY_NAME, MAILGUN_DOMAIN, MAILGUN_REGION, MAILGUN_SENDING_KEY, MAILGUN_WEBHOOK_SIGNING_KEY is bound on the Worker, outbound email is configured by it" (the seven names); both completed offline with exit 0, and neither needed Cloudflare credentials, although the README's deploy section still says the dry-run refuses without them. **Documentation — owner resets and the sole-workspace rule:** `OPERATIONS.md`, `docs/UI-PARITY.md` and `docs/account-security.md` now say what v0.4.21 enforces and left out: an owner's password-reset link and two-factor reset for a teammate work only while that owner's workspace holds the account's sole membership and the account does not administer the installation, otherwise the owner gets `409` until an owner of the other workspace removes the account there; with `MAIL_PROVIDER=none` `/forgot-password` answers `503` for such an account; hosted sign-in by the deployer works only for an owner or an admin. A regression test now covers the `409` and the reset that succeeds once the other workspace's owner removes the membership. **Migrations:** two since v0.4.21, applied once each, in this order, BEFORE the new Worker serves traffic: `324_scheduler_outbox_reads.sql`, then `325_knowledge_documents_version_url.sql`. Upgrade order is v0.4.21 -> v0.4.22: a v0.4.21 installation applies exactly these two (a v0.4.20 installation too, since v0.4.21 added none), and earlier installations first apply every missing published migration. Both are additive and index-only, with no row changes and nothing read, sent or queued: 324 creates seven indexes on conversation tags, the conversation outbox and workflow events (each builds in under a second on a large imported workspace), and 325 creates one index on `knowledge_documents (version_id, url)`. What an upgrading install should expect from 325: in the knowledge-index round, applying it to a real D1 database holding 3,154 documents read 7,721 rows, wrote 3,806 and took 109 ms; a far larger knowledge table (an installation that keeps many large crawl versions) was not measured, and the build cost grows with the number of documents, so back up D1 first and apply it before the Worker. After it, each crawled document writes one more row (6 written rows instead of 5 per document, 2,000 documents in 143 ms instead of 132 ms), and reads are unchanged.

What differs: text that was stored as plain words because it matched no help article when it was written, and matches one only now (an article published or edited later, for example a reply later turned into an article), is shown as stored to everyone who can read that conversation, instead of being replaced by "[Knowledge unavailable]" for a reader without access to that article; nothing stored changes. No migration. **Fixes — a conversation that holds references no longer reads every article of the workspace for each one, and a reference is found by its unique index:** when a teammate opens a conversation whose messages carry references (stored copies of help articles), the editor view looks up which articles each reference came from, and that lookup visited every article of the workspace (on a test workspace of 4,204 articles and 5,004 stored references, one open of a conversation with four references read about 36,000 rows). It now finds each article by its key (the same open reads about 2,400 rows; the lookup alone fell from 8,481 rows to 74). The lookup that stores a reference when text is written (messages, notes, replies, imports, answers) found its stored block by walking every block of the workspace and rescanning the request for each one; it now searches the unique workspace-and-fingerprint index once per block (35,312 rows read for six references among 5,004 blocks, now 14; a customer message that copies a help article reads about 3,800 rows instead of about 13,800). The rows returned, their order and every access check are unchanged, and a test runs the old and the new statements against the same data to prove it. What is not in this release: the conversation's attachment read still scans the attachment table, because no index covers the message it names; that needs a migration and waits for the next release. No migration. **rer 0.2.110 — the roster corner for a teammate erased by an older release is closed where HappyToHelp holds their hashed form, the managed-copy build issue REPORTS-001 is fixed, and the local key page changed:** the team adapter now names the older-release form of a roster address (`erased:` plus the SHA-256 of the lower-cased address, which v0.4.14 through v0.4.19 renamed an erased teammate's roster row to, and which v0.4.19 also stored as an inactive fence row at invite 0 for a teammate who was never on the roster), so a Business revision that lists a teammate erased by one of those releases by real address without a member id applies as retired (no fresh account, no invitation, no roster row) instead of the re-creation that the v0.4.20 and v0.4.21 notes describe as a known limit. What this does not cover: (1) a teammate erased before v0.4.14, which includes every teammate erased on production's v0.4.13 line, left no hashed form (the roster table first shipped in v0.4.14), so nothing recognises them from their address and a Business that lists them by address without a member id still creates a fresh account and an invitation; a Business that sends member ids fences them; (2) a teammate who was never on the roster and was erased by v0.4.19 is fenced only at invite 0, so a Business listing at invite 1 or higher admits them as a new person, as a larger invite number always does; (3) a person is recognised only under the address v0.4.19 stored for their roster row. The pin also fixes the managed-copy build (`rer check` no longer fails a managed copy of a published release for `.github/workflows` contract evidence it does not carry, REPORTS-001 on `.github/workflows/installer-journeys.yml`; proven on a synthetic managed copy with the platform's `rer-upstream.json`, not through a real platform build, and an install of an untagged commit keeps the check). The local key page (`/__dev/key`) now names the exact `rer dev` command to run, and the wording about the `/run` PATH changed; one known limit of that page: it tells a local owner who invited a teammate to run `rer dev --as <email>`, which HappyToHelp does not accept, because its local personas are the owner and signed-out only. Pins rer 0.2.110 and its Base copy. No migration. **Known limit — recovering an account that belongs to more than one workspace (still true in this release):** since v0.4.21 an owner changes a teammate's password or two-factor sign-in only where that workspace holds the account's sole membership. With outbound mail off (`MAIL_PROVIDER=none`), `/forgot-password` answers `503` for every account and sends nothing, so such an account cannot ask for a reset link by email, and the owner of either of its workspaces is refused with `409`; the deployer's hosted sign-in selects only an owner or an admin, so it does not help an operator-role teammate. An operator-role teammate in more than one workspace who has lost every second factor and recovery code has the same dead end with mail on or off, because `/forgot-password` changes only the password and an owner's two-factor reset is refused with `409` for such an account. The way out uses ordinary doors and keeps all support history (the removal drops the teammate's conversation follows and custom roles in that workspace, which its owner sets again): an owner of one of the account's workspaces removes it there (`DELETE /api/management/projects/<workspace id>/agents/<user id>`), the owner of the other workspace then issues the password-reset link or resets the two-factor sign-in, and the first workspace invites the teammate again. This release does not change the rule. **Correction to the v0.4.20 note on `rer deploy` and the mail secrets:** the v0.4.20 note said an offline `rer deploy --dry-run` lists the seven bound mail secret names and says the bound secrets were not read. That is what the dry-run prints with outbound mail off (`MAIL_PROVIDER=none`). Without any mail input (a new installation with `OWNER_EMAIL` only) it prints instead the production sign-in mail inputs a real deploy needs (`MAIL_PROVIDER`, `MAIL_FROM`, `EMAIL_API_KEY`) and still completes offline. Both shapes were run against this release's pinned rer 0.2.110: with `OWNER_EMAIL` only it printed that production sign-in mail line, and with `MAIL_PROVIDER=none` it printed "Outbound email is off (MAIL_PROVIDER=none) … The bound secrets were not read: if one of EMAIL_PROVIDER, EMAIL_FROM, EMAIL_API_KEY_NAME, MAILGUN_DOMAIN, MAILGUN_REGION, MAILGUN_SENDING_KEY, MAILGUN_WEBHOOK_SIGNING_KEY is bound on the Worker, outbound email is configured by it" (the seven names); both completed offline with exit 0, and neither needed Cloudflare credentials, although the README's deploy section still says the dry-run refuses without them. **Documentation — owner resets and the sole-workspace rule:** `OPERATIONS.md`, `docs/UI-PARITY.md` and `docs/account-security.md` now say what v0.4.21 enforces and left out: an owner's password-reset link and two-factor reset for a teammate work only while that owner's workspace holds the account's sole membership and the account does not administer the installation, otherwise the owner gets `409` until an owner of the other workspace removes the account there; with `MAIL_PROVIDER=none` `/forgot-password` answers `503` for such an account; hosted sign-in by the deployer works only for an owner or an admin. A regression test now covers the `409` and the reset that succeeds once the other workspace's owner removes the membership. **Migrations:** two since v0.4.21, applied once each, in this order, BEFORE the new Worker serves traffic: `324_scheduler_outbox_reads.sql`, then `325_knowledge_documents_version_url.sql`. Upgrade order is v0.4.21 -> v0.4.22: a v0.4.21 installation applies exactly these two (a v0.4.20 installation too, since v0.4.21 added none), and earlier installations first apply every missing published migration. Both are additive and index-only, with no row changes and nothing read, sent or queued: 324 creates seven indexes on conversation tags, the conversation outbox and workflow events (each builds in under a second on a large imported workspace), and 325 creates one index on `knowledge_documents (version_id, url)`. What an upgrading install should expect from 325: in the knowledge-index round, applying it to a real D1 database holding 3,154 documents read 7,721 rows, wrote 3,806 and took 109 ms; a far larger knowledge table (an installation that keeps many large crawl versions) was not measured, and the build cost grows with the number of documents, so back up D1 first and apply it before the Worker. After it, each crawled document writes one more row (6 written rows instead of 5 per document, 2,000 documents in 143 ms instead of 132 ms), and reads are unchanged.
